data.long_meaning: Sahebrao is a Sanskrit and Marathi name derived from the Sanskrit words saha (with) and brahman (god). The name means 'Owner of the Fort'. Sahebrao was a name borne by many Maratha kings and chieftains in Maharashtra. The name Sahebrao carries the meaning “Owner of the Fort” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Sahebrao usually hope their child will grow to embody owner of the fort and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Sahebrao belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Owner of the Fort.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Sahebrao total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: The name Sahebrao holds significant cultural impact in Maharashtra, as it was a name borne by many brave and powerful Maratha kings and chieftains. The name signified ownership or dominion over fortresses and was a symbol of power and strength. These Maratha rulers were known for their military prowess and contributions to Maharashtrian history. The name Sahebrao continues to be popular in Maharashtra and is a source of pride for many families.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Sahebrao lies in its Sanskrit roots, which signify being with or belonging to the divine. The name Brahman or God is an essential concept in Hinduism, and the name Sahebrao represents being a protector and an owner of the divine. It reminds one that true power and strength come from within, and being with God can provide one with the courage and resilience to overcome all challenges in life. Ultimately, the name Sahebrao inspires one to be a strong, courageous, and devout individual, who strives to be a protector, a leader, and a spiritual seeker.
